events.context: Assume users will keep software updated and follow documentation perfectly at runtime
Users deploy on cloud VMs with default settings, leaving ports open, diverging from plan
Over 237,000 instances exposed due to overconfidence in initial plan and lack of runtime adaptation
System listens on configured port (default 18789) without checking public interface or authentication
System responds to requests myopically, ignoring long-term security risks
RCE vulnerability (CVE-2026-25253) exploited via malicious link in WebSocket token handling
Flawed token validation allows arbitrary code execution, leading to compromise
OpenClaw becomes popular as high-autonomy agent runtime with integrations (Telegram/Slack/Feishu, email, filesystem, WebSocket)
Users adopt deployment pattern: Internet → OpenClaw instance → tools + local files + API keys, with port 18789 exposed publicly
Agents operate in ReAct-style loop: message → reasoning → tool execution → observation, accessing API keys, chat logs, filesystem
Attacker obtains token or WebSocket control channel, inputs instructions leading to agent execution
1. OpenClaw popular; 2. tutorials recommend quick deployment; 3. cloud users copy configs; 4. port exposed; 5. instances indexed by scanners, resulting in >230,000 exposed instances
